newsitem.title: CHINA: China accuses Taiwan of curbing contact with HK.
newsitem.headline: China accuses Taiwan of curbing contact with HK.

text.p: China on Friday accused rival Taiwan of curbing economic cooperation and contact between the island and Hong Kong, which reverted to Beijing's rule last week.

"We hope the Taiwan authorities... will not continue to serve as a passive force obstructing the development of Taiwan-Hong Kong relations and cross-Straits relations," the official Xinhua news agency said in a commentary carried in major newspapers.
Xinhua criticised Taiwan's new Hong Kong and Macau Relations Act, saying it "attempted to restrict and obstruct economic cooperation and contact between Hong Kong and Taiwan".
"This violates economic patterns and the desires and interests of Hong Kong and Taiwan compatriots," Xinhua said.
It did not say how the act restricted or obstructed cooperation and contact between Taiwan and the two territories.
Taiwan's parliament passed the act in March to govern the island's trade and other activities with Hong Kong and Macau after last week's handover of Hong Kong.

China resumed sovereignty over Hong Kong under a "one country, two systems" formula on July 1 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule. Macau will be handed back to Beijing on December 20, 1999, ending Portuguese control since 1557.

Under the "one country, two systems" formula devised by the late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, Beijing has promised to allow Hong Kong to keep its capitalist lifestyle for 50 years after the transfer to Chinese sovereignty.
China has wooed Taiwan to reunify under the same recovery formula and agreed to let the island keep its army.
But Taiwan's Nationalists, who lost the Chinese civil war to the Communists and fled into exile on the island in 1949, have rejected the formula, insisting on reunification under a democratic system.
Xinhua faulted Taiwan for rejecting the formula. "The Taiwan authorities have long distorted... the 'one country, two systems' (formula)," it said.
It said China was magnanimous, noting that Taiwan's offices and personnel in Hong Kong have been allowed to stay on after the handover. Xinhua warned them not to create disturbances in the territory.
China has neither restricted civilian exchanges nor banned air and shipping links between Hong Kong and Taiwan after the handover, Xinhua said.
"This demonstrates the goodwill and sincerity of the motherland... to maintain and develop Hong Kong-Taiwan civilian exchanges and relations," it said.
Xinhua urged Taiwan to reciprocate. "We hope the Taiwan authorities... will do more good things in the interest of Hong Kong and Taiwan compatriots," it said.

It said Taiwan had to recognise the reality of Hong Kong reverting to Beijing rule and maintain trade, air and mail links with the territory. Taiwan in 1949 banned direct trade, air and mail links with mainland China, but not Hong Kong.

Spelling out the new rules of the game, Xinhua said official contact, exchanges, negotiations, signing of agreements and the establishment of offices between Hong Kong and Taiwan in future would be arranged and handled by the Chinese central government.
